incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1753489123 - elevated gateway 5xx + timeouts detected (prod)

incident-bot: alerting channels: #incidents, paging sre-oncall-aaron, pager duty triggered

sre-oncall-aaron: saw it, I'm paging in eng-runtime-maya and carla-sre. Observability: 5xx spike started ~10:02 UTC, 5xx rate ~12% on /v1/embeddings/bulk, p95 latency > 5s.

eng-runtime-maya: joining. quick glance: Batcher queue depth for embedding-scheduler up ~6x, KV cache growth on gpu-pool-4, head-of-line blocking from several huge requests (payloads > 5k items).

carla-sre: can we confirm customer impact? support-liz please weigh in.

support-liz: CS: seeing ~28 customers with errors on UI, highest-tier customers get 503s intermittently, some calls timing out after 15s. I've flagged the top-3 customers, sending a short status note.

ben-ops: metric dump from 10:00-10:08: 
```
gateway.prod.requests.total = 128k
gateway.prod.errors.5xx = 15.5k
embedding.bulk.queue.depth = 240 -> baseline 40
gpu-pool-4.kvcache.size = 1.2GB -> baseline 200MB
batcher.processing.latency.p95 = 6.8s
```

eng-runtime-maya: looks like a sudden surge of bulk-embedding jobs (one client posted >10 concurrent 5k-item batches). This is filling the KV cache and blocking other smaller requests (head-of-line).

sre-oncall-aaron: immediate mitigations we can do: (1) throttle/429 large bulk-embed requests at gateway, (2) enable preemptive KV eviction on gpu-pool-4, (3) route enterprise keys to dedicated pool if available, (4) temporarily increase batcher concurrency for small requests. Will attempt 1 & 2 now.

infra-bot: running command: `rdwctl route update --service gateway --rule "if payload.size>2000 -> 429"`

infra-bot: route update applied (sha: a1b2c3).

eng-runtime-maya: applying preemptive eviction config to gpu-pool-4: `poolctl set kvcache.eviction_threshold=0.6`

infra-bot: kv eviction toggle succeeded on gpu-pool-4.

carla-sre: seeing immediate reduction in queue depth from 240 -> 110 and 5xx down from 12% -> 6% in last 45s. Small requests recovering.

support-liz: customer update: posted to customers A/B/C that we're throttling very large bulk requests to protect platform; ETA for fuller mitigation 30m.

product-john: any risk to SLAs? which customers hit SLA windows?

ben-ops: affected were non-enterprise first-party customers and a large embed consumer on free tier. No SLA violations flagged for enterprise-dedicated pools.

eng-runtime-maya: next step: identify noisy client and apply rate-limit by API key. Querying logs for top source IPs/keys.

eng-runtime-maya: found key k_9x7z — 11 concurrent bulk requests in last 3m. Proposing to rate-limit to 2 concurrent and shard their requests to slower path.

carla-sre: agree. apply soft limit with 429 and notify via email.

infra-bot: rate-limit rule applied for k_9x7z, concurrent=2, penalty window=60s.

incident-bot: automatic note: incident severity reduced from P0 -> P1 based on error rate and customer impact.

eng-runtime-maya: also enabling fallback path: route small/latency-sensitive calls to cpu-fallback-pool (lower cost but faster queueing). Command: `rdwctl routing add --selector "route=fastpath" --targets cpu-fallback-pool`

infra-bot: fastpath routing added, traffic split 90/10 to start.

carla-sre: p95 latencies for small requests now 300-400ms. 5xx down to 1.8%. Good.

sre-oncall-aaron: we'll keep throttling large bulk requests for next 2 hours and roll back eviction after KV stabilizes. Prepare a postmortem stub. Assigning owners: eng-runtime-maya root cause, carla-sre mitigation lead, support-liz customer comms.

product-john: please capture decision to throttle — we'll need a product note for API semantics and potential changes to bulk endpoint behavior.

eng-runtime-maya: creating follow-up tasks: (1) telemetry alert to detect large-parallel bulk submissions, (2) automatic backpressure at gateway for bulk endpoints, (3) improve KV TTL and per-key quota.

ben-ops: can we route enterprise traffic off gpu-pool-4 to dedicated-pool-2 to avoid collateral?

infra-bot: routing update: enterprise keys -> dedicated-pool-2 applied.

support-liz: posted customer-facing update: "We observed transient errors for some bulk embedding calls; we've throttled very large parallel jobs and performance is recovering. We'll follow up with details."

sre-oncall-aaron: preparing handoff to ops-next-oncall-zoe in 25m. Summary for handoff: cause - simultaneous large bulk-embed submissions overloaded batcher KV cache -> head-of-line blocking -> gateway 5xx/timeouts. Mitigations performed - throttled >2k payloads at gateway, set KV eviction, rate-limited noisy API key, enabled cpu fast-path, routed enterprise to dedicated pool. Current status - errors reduced to ~1.2%, queue depth stable ~45, customers impacted ~28 (mostly non-enterprise), escalation lowered.

ops-next-oncall-zoe: acknowledged, will monitor next 2 hrs and take ownership at 10:30 UTC. Any remaining runbook items?

carla-sre: please keep the route 429 rule in place until we have telemetry that bulk-queue depth < 50 for 15m.

eng-runtime-maya: logging note for postmortem: attach traces for k_9x7z and batcher backpressure timeline. Also include `rdwctl` commands used.

incident-bot: incident 1753489123 -> status: mitigated -> monitoring. Handoff recorded to ops-next-oncall-zoe. :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall-aaron: closing live paging. will populate postmortem draft after stabilization. Great job team. :thumbsup:
